summary.en: The Inca capital, which Pachacuti rebuilt in fitted stone around the Coricancha sun temple. Pizarro refounded it as a Spanish city in 1534; colonial churches and mansions rose on Inca walls. Peru’s 1993 constitution calls it the country’s historic capital.
summary.zh: 印加帝国首都，帕查库蒂围绕科里坎查太阳神殿用精密砌石将其重建。1534年皮萨罗将其重建为西班牙城市，殖民时代的教堂与宅邸建在印加石墙之上。秘鲁1993年宪法称其为国家的历史首都。

story.en:
Inca tradition said that Manco Capac founded Cusco where a golden staff sank into the earth. The city became an imperial capital in the 15th century, when Pachacuti is said to have rebuilt it in the shape of a puma, with the fortress-temple of Saqsaywaman as its head. Its heart was the Coricancha, whose walls the Spanish described as plated with sheets of gold.

Spaniards sent ahead in 1533 stripped gold from the Coricancha for Atahualpa’s ransom, and Pizarro’s army entered the city that November. The Dominicans built their monastery directly on the Coricancha, and the cathedral rose over the palace of Viracocha Inca. When an earthquake shook the city in 1950, much colonial masonry fell while the Inca walls beneath stood almost untouched.

Today Cusco is a UNESCO World Heritage city whose streets still follow the Inca plan. In 1990 the city authorities formally adopted the Quechua spelling Qosqo, though later administrations went back to Cusco.
story.zh:
印加传说称，曼科·卡帕克在一根金杖沉入大地之处建立了库斯科。15世纪这里成为帝国首都，据说帕查库蒂将城市重建为美洲狮的形状，萨克塞华曼要塞神庙即为狮首。城市的中心是科里坎查神殿，西班牙人记载其墙面覆有金板。

1533年，先行抵达的西班牙人从科里坎查剥下黄金充作阿塔瓦尔帕的赎金，同年11月皮萨罗的军队进入库斯科。多明我会直接在科里坎查之上修建修道院，大教堂则建在维拉科查·印卡的宫殿上。1950年地震时，大量殖民时期建筑倒塌，其下的印加石墙却几乎完好无损。

如今库斯科是联合国教科文组织世界遗产城市，街道仍沿袭印加时期的布局。1990年市政当局正式采用克丘亚语拼写 Qosqo，但此后的历届市政府又改回 Cusco。

sources.title: Britannica: Cuzco
UNESCO World Heritage: City of Cuzco
Brian S. Bauer, Ancient Cuzco: Heartland of the Inca (University of Texas Press, 2004)

note: The c. 1200 founding is traditional. The Spanish refoundation took place on 23 March 1534.

name.zh: 利马克（里马克河谷领地）

summary.en: Pizarro founded the “City of the Kings” on 18 January 1535 beside the Rímac river, near the seat of the local lord Taulichusco. As the viceregal capital it held the oldest chartered university in the Americas and the Inquisition; the Quechua-derived name Lima soon displaced the official one.
summary.zh: 1535年1月18日，皮萨罗在里马克河畔、当地首领陶利丘斯科的驻地附近建立“诸王之城”。作为总督区首都，这里有美洲最早获特许的大学和宗教裁判所；源自克丘亚语的“利马”之名很快取代了官方名称。

story.en:
Pizarro wanted a capital on the coast, close to the sea route to Panama and Spain, rather than in the Inca highlands. He chose the Rímac valley, already dotted with adobe pyramids such as Huaca Pucllana, and laid out a grid of 117 blocks around a main square. The founding date fell near the feast of the Epiphany, so the city was named for the Three Kings.

Lima grew rich on Potosí silver and became the seat of the viceroy, the archbishop, the university of San Marcos (1551) and, from 1570, the Inquisition. The earthquake and tsunami of 1746 destroyed most of the city and its port of Callao; Viceroy Manso de Velasco led the rebuilding.

San Martín proclaimed Peru’s independence in Lima’s main square on 28 July 1821. Its historic centre is now a World Heritage site.
story.zh:
皮萨罗希望把首都设在海岸，靠近通往巴拿马和西班牙的航线，而不是印加的高原。他选中了已散布着普克利亚纳等土坯金字塔的里马克河谷，围绕中央广场规划出117个街区的棋盘格。建城日期接近主显节，城市因此以“三王”命名。

利马因波托西白银而富庶，成为总督、大主教、圣马科斯大学（1551年）以及1570年起宗教裁判所的所在地。1746年地震与海啸摧毁了城市大部分地区及其港口卡亚俄，总督曼索·德·贝拉斯科主持了重建。

1821年7月28日，圣马丁在利马中央广场宣布秘鲁独立。其历史中心现为世界遗产。

sources.title: Britannica: Lima
UNESCO World Heritage: Historic Centre of Lima
Bernabé Cobo, Historia de la fundación de Lima (1639)

name.en: Bacatá (seat of the zipa, at Funza)
name.zh: 巴卡塔（西帕驻地，在今丰萨）

polity.zh: 新格拉纳达共和国 / 哥伦比亚

summary.en: Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada founded Santa Fe on 6 August 1538 in the territory of the Muisca zipa of Bacatá, whose name survives as Bogotá. The independent republic dropped “Santa Fe”; the 1991 constitution restored it as Santafé de Bogotá, and a 2000 amendment reverted to Bogotá.
summary.zh: 1538年8月6日，贡萨洛·希门尼斯·德·克萨达在穆伊斯卡西帕的巴卡塔领地上建立圣菲城，“巴卡塔”之名演变为“波哥大”。独立后共和国去掉了“圣菲”；1991年宪法恢复为“圣菲波哥大”，2000年修正案又改回“波哥大”。

story.en:
Jiménez de Quesada left Santa Marta in 1536 with about 800 men and struggled up the Magdalena river; fewer than 200 reached the cool Muisca plateau in 1537. They found a dense farming people who traded salt and emeralds, and after the death of the zipa Tisquesusa they founded Santa Fe at the foot of the eastern hills.

In 1539 two rival expeditions arrived almost at once: Nikolaus Federmann from Venezuela, working for the Welser bankers, and Sebastián de Belalcázar from Quito. The three captains avoided bloodshed and sailed to Spain to argue their claims, but the crown refused Quesada the governorship he sought, while Belalcázar received Popayán.

As capital of the New Kingdom of Granada and then of the viceroyalty, Santa Fe became a city of convents and of the Botanical Expedition led by José Celestino Mutis. Bolívar entered it after Boyacá in August 1819.
story.zh:
1536年，希门尼斯·德·克萨达率约800人离开圣玛尔塔，沿马格达莱纳河艰难溯流南下；1537年抵达凉爽的穆伊斯卡高原时已不足200人。他们发现这里是人口稠密的农耕民族，贸易盐和祖母绿；西帕蒂斯克苏萨死后，他们在东部山麓建立了圣菲城。

1539年，两支敌对的远征队几乎同时到达：一支是为韦尔泽银行家效力、从委内瑞拉而来的尼古拉斯·费德曼，另一支是从基多北上的塞巴斯蒂安·德·贝拉尔卡萨尔。三位首领避免了流血，一同赴西班牙申诉，但王室拒绝任命克萨达为他所求的总督，贝拉尔卡萨尔则获得了波帕扬。

作为新格拉纳达王国及后来总督区的首都，圣菲成为修道院林立、何塞·塞莱斯蒂诺·穆蒂斯植物考察队所在的城市。1819年8月博亚卡战役后，玻利瓦尔进入此城。

sources.title: Britannica: Bogotá
Juan Friede, Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada a través de documentos históricos (1960)
Constitution of Colombia (1991), art. 322, and Legislative Act 01 of 2000

note: Bacatá, the zipa’s seat, lay at present-day Funza on the Sabana, about 20 km west of the colonial city.

name.zh: 拉普拉塔 / 丘基萨卡

polity.en: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata

summary.en: Founded as La Plata around 1538 near the Indigenous settlement of Chuquisaca, the city was the seat of the Audiencia of Charcas and of a famous university. Bolivia’s independence was declared here in 1825; in 1839 it was renamed after Antonio José de Sucre.
summary.zh: 约1538年在原住民聚落丘基萨卡附近建立，名为拉普拉塔，是查尔卡斯检审庭和一所著名大学的所在地。1825年玻利维亚在此宣布独立；1839年以安东尼奥·何塞·德·苏克雷之名改称苏克雷。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Historic City of Sucre
Britannica: Sucre
Herbert S. Klein, A Concise History of Bolivia (Cambridge UP, 2003)

note: Founding is variously dated 1538–1540. The city was also called Charcas in colonial usage.

polity.en: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata

summary.en: A mining camp at 4,000 m below the Cerro Rico grew within decades into one of the largest cities of the Americas. Charles V granted it the title Villa Imperial in 1547. Its mint, the Casa de la Moneda, struck the silver coins that circulated from Seville to Manila.
summary.zh: 海拔4000米的里科山下的矿营在数十年内发展为美洲最大的城市之一。查理五世于1547年授予其“帝国镇”称号。城中造币厂铸造的银币流通于从塞维利亚到马尼拉的广大地区。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: City of Potosí
Kris Lane, Potosí: The Silver City That Changed the World (University of California Press, 2019)
Columbia University, “The Silver Mine” (Hispanic collection essay)

note: The Villa Imperial title is usually dated to a royal decree of 28 January 1547; some sources give 1553.

name.en: São Sebastião do Rio de Janeiro
name.zh: 圣塞巴斯蒂昂-杜里约热内卢

polity.en: United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves
polity.zh: 葡萄牙、巴西及阿尔加维联合王国

summary.en: Portuguese sailors named Guanabara Bay the “River of January” in 1502. Estácio de Sá founded São Sebastião do Rio de Janeiro on 1 March 1565 to expel French colonists. It became Brazil’s colonial capital in 1763, the seat of the Portuguese crown from 1808 and the national capital until Brasília opened in 1960.
summary.zh: 1502年葡萄牙水手把瓜纳巴拉湾称作“一月之河”。1565年3月1日，埃斯塔西奥·德·萨为驱逐法国殖民者建立圣塞巴斯蒂昂-杜里约热内卢。1763年成为巴西殖民地首府，1808年起为葡萄牙王室驻地，直至1960年巴西利亚启用前一直是国家首都。

story.en:
The first Europeans to enter Guanabara Bay, in January 1502, took it for the mouth of a river, and the name Rio de Janeiro stuck. In 1555 the French admiral Nicolas Durand de Villegaignon fortified an island there for “France Antarctique”, a colony that also sheltered Huguenots.

Estácio de Sá, nephew of governor-general Mem de Sá, founded a Portuguese settlement at the foot of the Sugarloaf on 1 March 1565 and named it for Saint Sebastian and King Sebastião. He died of an arrow wound in the battle that drove out the French in 1567, and the city moved to the Morro do Castelo.

Gold from Minas Gerais flowed out through Rio, so in 1763 the capital moved here from Salvador. When the Portuguese court fled Napoleon in 1808, Rio became the only European royal capital outside Europe, and it stayed Brazil’s capital until 1960.
story.zh:
1502年1月，最早驶入瓜纳巴拉湾的欧洲人误以为这是一条河的入海口，“里约热内卢”（一月之河）之名由此沿用。1555年，法国海军将领维尔加尼翁在湾内一座岛上筑堡，建立“南极法兰西”殖民地，并收容胡格诺派教徒。

1565年3月1日，总督门·德·萨的侄子埃斯塔西奥·德·萨在面包山脚下建立葡萄牙定居点，以圣塞巴斯蒂安和塞巴斯蒂昂国王之名命名。1567年他在驱逐法国人的战斗中中箭身亡，城市随后迁至城堡山。

米纳斯吉拉斯的黄金经里约外运，1763年首府因此由萨尔瓦多迁来。1808年葡萄牙王室为躲避拿破仑逃到这里，里约成为唯一一座位于欧洲以外的欧洲王国首都，并一直作为巴西首都至1960年。

sources.title: Britannica: Rio de Janeiro
UNESCO World Heritage: Rio de Janeiro: Carioca Landscapes between the Mountain and the Sea
Boris Fausto, A Concise History of Brazil (Cambridge UP, 1999)

name.en: São Salvador da Bahia de Todos os Santos
name.zh: 圣萨尔瓦多-达巴伊亚-德托多斯奥斯桑托斯

name.en: São Salvador da Bahia de Todos os Santos
name.zh: 圣萨尔瓦多-达巴伊亚-德托多斯奥斯桑托斯

summary.en: Tomé de Sousa founded Salvador on the Bay of All Saints in 1549 as the seat of Brazil’s first royal government. For two centuries it was the colonial capital and the main port of the sugar economy and the Atlantic slave trade, and it is often called the most African city of the Americas.
summary.zh: 1549年托梅·德·索萨在诸圣湾畔建立萨尔瓦多，作为巴西首个王室政府的驻地。两个世纪里，它是殖民地首府，也是蔗糖经济和大西洋奴隶贸易的主要港口，常被称为美洲非洲文化色彩最浓的城市。

story.en:
In 1549 King João III placed Brazil’s failing private captaincies under a royal government. Tomé de Sousa arrived with about a thousand men, including the first Jesuits under Manuel da Nóbrega, and built a walled city on a cliff above the bay, with an upper town for government and churches and a lower town for the port.

The Dutch West India Company captured Salvador in May 1624, but a Spanish–Portuguese fleet of more than fifty ships retook it in April 1625. Sugar from the Recôncavo plantations made Salvador one of the richest cities in the Portuguese world, and hundreds of thousands of enslaved Africans landed at its docks.

The capital moved to Rio in 1763, but Salvador kept its baroque churches and its African heritage, visible in Candomblé, capoeira and cuisine. Its historic centre, the Pelourinho, is a World Heritage site.
story.zh:
1549年，若昂三世设立王室政府，统辖经营不善的私人受封领地。托梅·德·索萨率约千人抵达，其中包括曼努埃尔·达·诺布雷加带领的第一批耶稣会士，在海湾上方的悬崖上修建了带城墙的城市：上城为官署与教堂，下城为港口。

1624年5月荷兰西印度公司攻占萨尔瓦多，但1625年4月一支五十余艘战舰的西葡联合舰队将其夺回。雷孔卡沃种植园的蔗糖使萨尔瓦多成为葡萄牙世界最富庶的城市之一，数十万被奴役的非洲人在此登岸。

1763年首府迁往里约，但萨尔瓦多保留了巴洛克教堂和非洲文化遗产，体现在坎东布雷教、卡波耶拉和饮食之中。其历史中心佩洛里尼奥为世界遗产。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Historic Centre of Salvador de Bahia
Britannica: Salvador
Stuart B. Schwartz, Sugar Plantations in the Formation of Brazilian Society: Bahia, 1550–1835 (Cambridge UP, 1985)

name.zh: 圣玛利亚-德尔布恩艾雷（1541年废弃）

name.en: Ciudad de la Santísima Trinidad y Puerto de Santa María de los Buenos Aires
name.zh: 至圣三一城与圣玛利亚好风港

polity.en: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
United Provinces of the Río de la Plata / Argentine Confederation
polity.zh: 拉普拉塔联合省 / 阿根廷邦联

summary.en: Pedro de Mendoza’s settlement of 1536 starved and was abandoned in 1541; Juan de Garay refounded the city from Asunción in 1580. A smuggling port for Potosí silver, it became a viceregal capital in 1776 and Argentina’s federal capital in 1880.
summary.zh: 佩德罗·德·门多萨1536年建立的定居点因饥荒于1541年被弃；1580年胡安·德·加拉伊从亚松森南下重建此城。它曾是波托西白银的走私港，1776年成为总督区首府，1880年成为阿根廷联邦首都。

story.en:
Pedro de Mendoza arrived in 1536 with one of the largest fleets yet sent to the Americas. His settlement on the Río de la Plata was besieged by the Querandí and ravaged by hunger; the German soldier Ulrich Schmidl, who was there, described men eating leather and worse. Mendoza sailed for Spain and died at sea, and the last settlers withdrew to Asunción in 1541.

In 1580 Juan de Garay came downriver from Asunción with about sixty settlers, most of them born in the Americas, and refounded the city on 11 June. Horses left behind by the first settlers had reportedly multiplied across the pampas.

For two centuries Spain forced trade through Lima, so Buenos Aires lived by contraband. Its fortunes turned in 1776, when it became the capital of the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata, and in 1880 it was federalised as Argentina’s capital.
story.zh:
1536年，佩德罗·德·门多萨率领当时派往美洲规模最大的船队之一抵达。他在拉普拉塔河畔的定居点遭克兰迪人围困、饥荒肆虐；亲历其事的德意志士兵乌尔里希·施米德尔记载人们以皮革乃至更可怕的东西果腹。门多萨启程返西，死于海上，最后一批移民于1541年撤往亚松森。

1580年，胡安·德·加拉伊率约六十名移民（多为美洲出生者）从亚松森顺流而下，于6月11日重建此城。据说首批移民遗弃的马匹已在潘帕斯草原上大量繁衍。

两个世纪里西班牙强制贸易经由利马，布宜诺斯艾利斯靠走私为生。1776年它成为新设的拉普拉塔总督区首府，命运由此转变；1880年被划为联邦区，成为阿根廷首都。

sources.title: Britannica: Buenos Aires
Ulrich Schmidl, Wahrhaftige Historien einer wunderbaren Schiffart (1567)
James R. Scobie, Buenos Aires: Plaza to Suburb, 1870–1910 (Oxford UP, 1974)

polity.en: Governorate of New Castile / Viceroyalty of Peru
polity.zh: 新卡斯蒂利亚省 / 秘鲁总督区

polity.en: Real Audiencia of Quito (Viceroyalty of Peru)
polity.zh: 基多检审庭（秘鲁总督区）

summary.en: A northern Inca centre favoured by Huayna Capac, Quito was burned by Atahualpa’s general Rumiñahui before Sebastián de Belalcázar refounded it on 6 December 1534. Its colonial churches made it, with Kraków, the first city inscribed on the World Heritage List in 1978.
summary.zh: 基多是瓦伊纳·卡帕克所钟爱的印加北方重镇，1534年12月6日塞巴斯蒂安·德·贝拉尔卡萨尔重建之前，曾被阿塔瓦尔帕的将领鲁米尼亚维焚毁。其殖民时期教堂使它与克拉科夫一起，于1978年成为首批列入世界遗产名录的城市。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: City of Quito
Britannica: Quito
Pedro Cieza de León, Crónica del Perú, part I (1553)

note: The Inca conquest of the Quito region under Topa Inca is dated only approximately (1460s).

name.zh: 圣地亚哥-德莱昂-德加拉加斯

polity.zh: 委内瑞拉省（西班牙帝国）

polity.en: First and Second Venezuelan Republics / royalist Venezuela
polity.zh: 委内瑞拉第一、第二共和国 / 保王派控制

summary.en: Diego de Losada founded Santiago de León de Caracas in a mountain valley in 1567, naming it after a local Indigenous people. Capital of the Captaincy General from 1777, it was Bolívar’s birthplace and the city where Venezuela declared independence on 5 July 1811.
summary.zh: 1567年迭戈·德·洛萨达在一处山谷中建立圣地亚哥-德莱昂-德加拉加斯，以当地一个原住民族群命名。1777年起为都督府首府，是玻利瓦尔的出生地，委内瑞拉于1811年7月5日在此宣布独立。

sources.title: Britannica: Caracas
UNESCO World Heritage: Ciudad Universitaria de Caracas
John V. Lombardi, Venezuela: The Search for Order, the Dream of Progress (Oxford UP, 1982)

name.en: Nuestra Señora Santa María de la Asunción

polity.en: Governorate of the Río de la Plata
Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata

summary.en: Founded as a fort on 15 August 1537, the feast of the Assumption, Asunción was for decades the main Spanish base in the Río de la Plata and is called the “mother of cities” because expeditions from it founded Santa Fe, Buenos Aires and others. Spanish–Guaraní unions there shaped Paraguay’s bilingual society.
summary.zh: 1537年8月15日（圣母升天节）作为要塞建立，数十年间是西班牙在拉普拉塔地区的主要据点，因圣菲、布宜诺斯艾利斯等城皆由此出发的远征队所建而被称为“众城之母”。西班牙人与瓜拉尼人的结合塑造了巴拉圭的双语社会。

sources.title: Britannica: Asunción
Branislava Susnik, El indio colonial del Paraguay (1965)
Wikipedia: Asunción

summary.en: Pedro de Valdivia founded Santiago del Nuevo Extremo on 12 February 1541 at the foot of Santa Lucía hill, on land of the Inca-influenced Mapocho valley. Within months the Mapuche leader Michimalonco burned it to the ground; Inés de Suárez’s defence became a founding legend.
summary.zh: 1541年2月12日，佩德罗·德·瓦尔迪维亚在圣卢西亚山脚、受印加影响的马波乔河谷中建立“新端圣地亚哥”。数月后马普切首领米奇马隆科将其焚毁，伊内斯·德·苏亚雷斯的守城事迹成为建城传奇。

sources.title: Britannica: Santiago
Pedro de Valdivia, Cartas de relación de la conquista de Chile (1545–1552)
Wikipedia: Santiago

name.zh: 累西腓 / 毛里茨斯塔德

summary.en: Named for the reef that shelters its harbour, Recife was the port of Olinda until the Dutch made it the capital of New Holland. Johan Maurits laid out Mauritsstad on Antônio Vaz island with bridges and palaces, and the first synagogue in the Americas, Kahal Zur Israel, opened here.
summary.zh: 累西腓因护卫港湾的礁石而得名，原为奥林达的港口，后被荷兰人定为新荷兰首府。约翰·毛里茨在安东尼奥·瓦斯岛上规划了建有桥梁与宫殿的毛里茨斯塔德，美洲第一座犹太会堂“以色列之石”也在此开放。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Recife
C. R. Boxer, The Dutch in Brazil, 1624–1654 (Clarendon Press, 1957)
Britannica: Recife

note: Recife became the capital of Pernambuco only in 1827; under the Dutch it was the colonial capital.

name.en: São José da Barra do Rio Negro (Lugar da Barra)
name.zh: 内格罗河口圣若泽（巴拉）

name.en: Cidade da Barra do Rio Negro

summary.en: A Portuguese fort of 1669 at the meeting of the Rio Negro and the Solimões grew into the capital of Amazonas. Named after the Manaó people, it became the opulent hub of the rubber boom, with electric trams and the Teatro Amazonas opera house (1896).
summary.zh: 1669年葡萄牙人在内格罗河与索利蒙伊斯河交汇处修建的要塞，后发展为亚马孙州首府。城市以马瑙人命名，在橡胶繁荣期成为奢华的中心，拥有电车和亚马孙剧院（1896年）。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Manaus
Barbara Weinstein, The Amazon Rubber Boom, 1850–1920 (Stanford UP, 1983)
Britannica: Manaus

name.en: Santo Tomé de Guayana de Angostura
name.zh: 安戈斯图拉（圣托梅-德瓜亚那）

polity.zh: 委内瑞拉共和国（玻利瓦尔的临时首都）

summary.en: A Spanish river town at a narrows (“angostura”) of the Orinoco, it was Bolívar’s base after 1817. The Congress of Angostura met here in 1819 and proclaimed the Republic of Colombia; the city took Bolívar’s name in 1846. Angostura bitters were first made here.
summary.zh: 西班牙人在奥里诺科河狭窄处（angostura）建立的河港，1817年后成为玻利瓦尔的根据地。1819年安戈斯图拉国会在此召开并宣告哥伦比亚共和国成立；1846年城市改以玻利瓦尔命名。安戈斯图拉苦精即诞生于此。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Ciudad Bolívar
Britannica: Ciudad Bolívar
John Lynch, Simón Bolívar: A Life (Yale UP, 2006)

polity.en: New Kingdom of Granada (Viceroyalty of Peru)
polity.zh: 新格拉纳达王国（秘鲁总督区）
西班牙帝国（保王派收复）

summary.en: Pedro de Heredia founded Cartagena in 1533 on a bay he likened to Cartagena in Spain. Ringed by the strongest fortifications in Spanish America, it was a treasure-fleet port and a main slave market, where Pedro Claver ministered to enslaved Africans. It declared absolute independence in November 1811.
summary.zh: 1533年佩德罗·德·埃雷迪亚在一处他认为酷似西班牙卡塔赫纳的海湾建城。城市环绕着西属美洲最坚固的防御工事，是珍宝船队港口和主要奴隶市场，佩德罗·克拉韦尔曾在此为被奴役的非洲人服务。1811年11月宣布完全独立。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Port, Fortresses and Group of Monuments, Cartagena
Britannica: Cartagena
Anthony McFarlane, Colombia before Independence (Cambridge UP, 1993)

name.en: San Felipe y Santiago de Montevideo
name.zh: 圣费利佩-圣地亚哥-德蒙得维的亚

polity.en: Governorate of the Río de la Plata (Viceroyalty of Peru)
polity.zh: 拉普拉塔省（秘鲁总督区）

polity.en: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata

polity.zh: 联合省 / 阿蒂加斯联邦同盟
葡属及巴西西斯普拉蒂纳省

summary.en: The Spanish governor Bruno Mauricio de Zabala fortified Montevideo from 1724 to stop Portuguese expansion from Colonia. A royalist naval base during the independence wars, it was the capital of Brazil’s Cisplatina province before becoming capital of independent Uruguay in 1828.
summary.zh: 1724年起西班牙总督布鲁诺·毛里西奥·德·萨瓦拉在蒙得维的亚筑城设防，以阻止葡萄牙人从科洛尼亚扩张。独立战争期间它是保王派的海军基地，曾为巴西西斯普拉蒂纳省首府，1828年起成为独立的乌拉圭首都。

sources.title: Britannica: Montevideo
Lindsay Lyons, Uruguay: A History (Oxford UP, 2002)
Wikipedia: Montevideo

note: Founding is dated 1724 (fortification) to 1726 (formal founding with settlers).

polity.zh: 英属苏里南殖民地（威洛比兰）

name.zh: 帕拉马里博（泽兰迪亚堡）

summary.en: Near an Indigenous village on the Suriname river, English settlers built a fort in 1650 that a Zeeland fleet captured in 1667 and renamed Fort Zeelandia. Paramaribo became the capital of a Dutch plantation colony worked by enslaved Africans until abolition in 1863, and in 1975 of independent Suriname. Its wooden inner city is a World Heritage site.
summary.zh: 英国殖民者于1650年在苏里南河畔一个原住民村落附近筑堡，1667年泽兰舰队攻占此地，改名泽兰迪亚堡。帕拉马里博随后成为荷兰种植园殖民地的首府，那里依靠被奴役的非洲人劳作，直到1863年废奴；1975年它成为独立的苏里南首都。其木构内城是世界遗产。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Historic Inner City of Paramaribo
Britannica: Paramaribo
Wikipedia: Paramaribo

note: The Treaty of Breda (1667) confirmed Dutch possession of Suriname while England kept New Amsterdam. Britain occupied the colony in 1799–1802 and 1804–1816.
